hypotheses: finite declared primitive candidate universe and exact complete point/candidate graph
same global dead, forced and earliest-generation scheduler
hints change ordering only; every domain member retained in stable fallback
branch-local exclusions only after complete exhausted child; unknown is never exclusion
exact graph and hint rollback; full identity and aggregate markings preserve shared placements

claims.name: Hint ordering preserves one-step domain
claims.statement: For the selected point \(p\), the preferred-plus-fallback sequence is a permutation of \(D_p(S,X)\).
claims.argument: Take eligible legal preferred keys once; then enumerate every base-domain key not already seen. No hint mutates graph domains. Hence no illegal, duplicate or omitted key enters the resulting sequence.

claims.name: Hints preserve reference point and propagation
claims.statement: The chosen point and dead/forced/branch kind depend on the unchanged complete graph, before hint ordering.
claims.argument: Compute graph decision first. Forced moves use the graph singleton, even if a hint is waiting or retired. Branch hints can only reorder the selected domain.

claims.name: Whole-hint retirement preserves base alternatives
claims.statement: Retirement removes continuation preferences, without proving any constituent impossible.
claims.argument: An invalid pending cluster may have legal siblings. Retire its whole preference contribution while the unchanged graph continues to expose those siblings through complete fallback.

claims.name: Finite search preserves existence and exhaustion
claims.statement: Subject to the hypotheses and no budget cutoff, first-success DFS preserves existence of a finite exact solution and the soundness of finite exhaustion. Exhaustive enumeration would retain the same exact solution set.
claims.argument: Every branch domain is fully available, point legality is unchanged, and an excluded child has been completely exhausted in that exact parent state. Induct on finite remaining occupancy/placements; rollback restores the parent. First-success DFS may return a different solution and does not enumerate every solution. A budget cutoff establishes unknown only.

scope: These are host arguments about ordering infrastructure, not native proof certificates, universal theorem-language completeness, an infinite-plane tiling theorem, measured speedup, or a theorem discovered by the new executor.
independent_wording_correction: Clarified that first-success DFS does not literally visit the entire solution set; exact exhaustive enumeration is a distinct algorithm.
